breakfast.name: Canjeero (Sourdough Pancake)
instructions: Mix batter, ferment 1 hour
Pour thin circle on hot griddle
Cook until holes form
Serve with butter, sugar, or stew
breakfast.description: Spongy sourdough pancake — Somalia's daily bread.

breakfast.name: Sabaayad (Flatbread)
instructions: Make dough, rest
Roll, spread oil, fold layers
Roll again, cook on griddle
Brush with butter

breakfast.name: Canjeero with Maraq
ingredients: Canjeero (Somali sour flatbread -- fermented teff or sorghum batter)
Maraq (Somali spiced broth -- lamb or goat with cardamom, cloves, cinnamon)
instructions: Canjeero is the Somali fermented flatbread -- similar to the Ethiopian injera but smaller and crispier
Made from fermented teff or sorghum batter
Cooked on a flat pan until the holes form on the surface
Maraq: the Somali broth -- lamb or goat simmered with warm spices
The canjeero is dipped into the hot maraq
The combination of the sour bread and the spiced broth is the Somali breakfast
breakfast.description: Somali fermented flatbread with spiced broth -- canjeero (smaller and crispier than Ethiopian injera, made from fermented teff or sorghum) dipped into maraq (lamb or goat broth spiced with cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon). The Somali breakfast combination.

breakfast.name: Xawaash Spiced Tea
ingredients: Xawaash spice mix (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, black pepper)
instructions: Xawaash is the Somali spice blend -- used in tea and cooking
The same warm spices as the Indian chai blend -- via Arab trade routes
Brewed strong with the spices
Milk and sugar added
The Somali tea culture: hospitality expressed through offering tea
Cardamom is the dominant spice in Somali tea
breakfast.description: Somali spiced tea -- black tea brewed with xawaash (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, black pepper), sweetened, served with milk. Cardamom is the dominant spice. The Somali tea is the hospitality gesture: offering tea to a guest.

lunch.name: Bariis Iskukaris (Spiced Rice)
ingredients: Xawaash spice (cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves)
instructions: Brown meat with onion and garlic
Add xawaash spice
Add rice and water
Cook covered until done
Top with raisins
lunch.description: Fragrant Somali spiced rice with meat.

lunch.name: Suqaar (Diced Meat)
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic
Add meat, brown
Add peppers and tomatoes
Cook until done
Serve with canjeero or rice

lunch.name: Cambuulo (Adzuki Beans with Sesame)
instructions: Cambuulo is the Somali bean dish -- adzuki beans with sesame
The adzuki beans are a Somali and East African staple
Cooked until soft and then dressed with sesame oil
Sweetened slightly -- the sweet-savory combination
A distinctive Somali flavor: legumes with sesame oil and a touch of sweetness
lunch.description: Somali adzuki beans with sesame -- small red adzuki beans cooked until soft, dressed with sesame oil and a touch of sugar or dates. The sesame oil and slight sweetness with legumes is a distinctive Somali flavor combination.

lunch.name: Hilib Ari (Goat Stew)
instructions: Hilib ari (goat stew) is the everyday Somali protein dish
Goat is the most common meat in Somali cuisine
Braised with onion, tomatoes, and xawaash spices
The green chillis add fresh heat
Served with rice or canjeero
lunch.description: Somali goat stew -- goat on the bone braised with onion, tomatoes, xawaash spice mix (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves), and green chillis. Goat is the dominant Somali meat. Served with rice or canjeero.

lunch.name: Bariis Iskukaris (Somali Spiced Rice)
ingredients: Xawaash (Somali spice blend: cardamom, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, black pepper)
instructions: Bariis iskukaris is the Somali spiced rice -- the equivalent of biryani
The Arabic influence on Somali food: spiced rice is an Arab contribution
Somalia has centuries of Arab trade and cultural exchange
The rice is cooked in the spiced stock
Xawaash is the Somali equivalent of the Indian garam masala
Served alongside goat, chicken, or fish
lunch.description: Somali aromatic spiced rice -- basmati cooked in xawaash-spiced stock (cardamom, cumin, coriander, cinnamon) with ghee. The Arab trade influence on Somali food: Somalia had centuries of Arab cultural exchange that shaped its spice use. Served with goat, chicken, or fish.

dinner.name: Hilib Ari (Goat Stew)
instructions: Brown goat meat
Add onion, garlic, tomatoes, xawaash
Add water, simmer 45 min
Add potatoes, cook until tender
dinner.description: Slow-simmered goat stew with Somali spices.

dinner.name: Muufo (Corn Flatbread)
instructions: Mix cornmeal with flour and water
Shape thick rounds
Cook on griddle until browned
Serve with stew

dinner.name: Nafaqo (Banana Fritters)
instructions: Nafaqo are Somali banana fritters -- spiced with cardamom
The ripe bananas are mashed into a batter
Cardamom is the essential spice -- the Somali flavor
Fried until golden
Eaten as a snack or dessert
dinner.description: Somali banana fritters -- ripe bananas mashed into a cardamom-spiced batter and fried golden. Cardamom is the essential Somali flavor in sweet preparations.

dinner.name: Muufo (Cornbread)
instructions: Muufo is the Somali cornbread -- cooked on a flat griddle
Thin, flat cornbread with a slightly crispy exterior
Sesame seeds sometimes pressed onto the surface
Eaten with butter, ghee, or tea
A simple and ancient Somali bread
dinner.description: Somali cornbread -- thin flat cornmeal bread cooked on a griddle with sesame seeds, eaten with ghee or tea. A simple ancient Somali staple.

dinner.name: Camel Meat (Hilibka Geel)
instructions: Camel meat is eaten in Somalia -- one of the few countries where it is a regular food
The camel is a central animal in Somali pastoralist culture
Camel milk is also drunk daily -- very nutritious
The meat is tougher and gamier than beef -- needs long cooking
Braised for 2+ hours with xawaash spices
A mark of celebration and generosity
dinner.description: Somali camel meat stew -- one of the few cuisines where camel meat is regularly eaten. Braised for 2+ hours with xawaash spices, onion, and tomatoes. The camel is central to Somali pastoralist culture (milk drunk daily; meat at celebrations). Tougher and gamier than beef, needing long cooking.

snacks.name: Sambusa
ingredients: Filling: spiced ground beef, onion, chili
instructions: Make dough strips, fold triangles with filling
Fry until golden

snacks.name: Halwa (Somali Sweet)
instructions: Somali halwa is different from Turkish or Arab halwa -- it is a dense, gelatinous sweet
The starch is cooked with sugar and ghee until it forms a translucent, rubbery candy
Cardamom and rosewater flavor it
Saffron gives the yellow color
Halwa is made and sold at celebrations: weddings, Eid
Every Somali city has its halwa vendors
snacks.description: Somali gelatinous sweet -- cornstarch cooked with sugar and ghee until translucent and rubbery (not the Middle Eastern sesame type), flavored with cardamom, rosewater, and saffron. Made for weddings and Eid; sold by vendors in every Somali city.

snacks.name: Dates with Tea
instructions: Dates are the Islamic world food of hospitality
Somalia: an overwhelmingly Muslim country -- dates are eaten daily
The Prophet Muhammad broke his fast with dates
Dates with tea: the Somali everyday snack
The sweetness of dates pairs with the spiced tea
snacks.description: Somali dates with spiced tea -- dried dates (the Islamic world food of hospitality) eaten alongside cardamom-spiced tea. Somalia is overwhelmingly Muslim; dates are eaten daily and at every gathering.

snacks.name: Roasted Corn (Galees)
instructions: Roasted corn is a Somali street snack
Cooked over charcoal
The kernels slightly char
Salted and eaten hot
snacks.description: Somali roasted corn -- corn on the cob charcoal-grilled until slightly charred, salted. Street snack sold throughout Somalia.

desserts.name: Halwo (Halva)
instructions: Make sugar syrup
Cook cornstarch with butter
Gradually add syrup, stirring constantly
Add spices
Pour into mold, let set

desserts.name: Xalwa (Sweet Sesame Candy)
instructions: Sesame candy is a Somali sweet -- sesame cooked in caramelized sugar
The sesame seeds are coated in caramelized sugar
Set into bars or clusters
Cardamom adds the warm Somali spice note
desserts.description: Somali sesame candy -- roasted sesame seeds cooked in caramelized sugar, set into bars. Cardamom optional. A simple, nutty Somali sweet.

desserts.name: Bur (Fried Dough with Honey)
instructions: Bur is the Somali fried dough -- drizzled with honey or date syrup
A simple yeast dough fried until golden
Drizzled with date syrup or honey when warm
A sweet conclusion to a meal or celebration
desserts.description: Somali fried honey dough -- yeast dough fried until golden and drizzled with honey or date syrup while warm. A simple Somali sweet eaten after meals or at celebrations.

drinks.name: Shaah Cadeys (Somali Tea)
instructions: Boil tea with spices
Add milk and sugar
Strain

drinks.name: Shaah Bun (Coffee-Spice Tea)
instructions: Brew coffee with spices
Strain, sweeten
drinks.description: Unique coffee-spice brew — halfway between tea and coffee.

drinks.name: Camel Milk
instructions: Camel milk is drunk daily in Somali pastoralist culture
Nutritionally superior to cow milk: more vitamin C, iron, and lower lactose
The camel is the central animal of Somali nomadic life
Fresh camel milk: slightly salty, thin, with a slightly unusual flavor compared to cow milk
Also fermented into a sour camel milk (suusac)
Nomadic Somalis survive on camel milk alone during dry seasons
drinks.description: Somali fresh camel milk -- drunk daily in Somali pastoralist culture. Nutritionally superior to cow milk: more vitamin C, lower lactose. Slightly salty and thin. Nomadic Somalis survive on camel milk during dry seasons. Also fermented into suusac (sour camel milk).
